Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):
  - Acute shortness of breath onset ~1 hour while sitting watching TV.
  - Cough started yesterday; non-productive (patient reports no sputum).
  - Palpitations/subjective increased heart rate.
  - Chest soreness on deep inspiration; chest wall and C‑section scar tenderness.
  - Recent obstetric history: lower-segment Caesarean section 4 weeks ago.
  - No other chronic medical problems reported.
  - Allergy: ibuprofen (reaction not described).

- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):
  - Mother has history of clots in legs (venous thromboembolism).

- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:
  - Codeine — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient reports using fairly regularly after C‑section; states probably has not taken it for one week).
  - No other medications, traditional or OTC documented.

- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):
  - Not recorded.

- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:
  - Postpartum, 4 weeks following C‑section; currently with baby.
  - Breastfeeding/contraception status not documented.

- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:
  - Not recorded. Patient reports she “gets coughs and colds quite a lot.”

- Hearing and vision concerns:
  - Not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):
  - Patient reports feeling stressed/anxious due to palpitations and shortness of breath.
  - No suicidal ideation or other mental health history documented.

- Social context: family support, caregiving, housing, financial stressors:
  - Partner at work; patient alone at home at time of consult.
  - Patient will take baby and go to hospital; no other supports or social stressors documented.

Examination

- Vital signs: BP, pulse rate and rhythm:
  - No formal vital signs recorded (BP, RR, SpO2, temperature not documented).
  - Pulse: clinician instructed patient to palpate radial pulse and count beats; patient reported “30” (timing/duration of count not documented). Clinician noted heart rate “slightly fast” at time of exam. (Timing/interval for pulse count not documented — uncertainty noted.)

- Anthropometry: height, weight, BMI, waist circumference:
  - Not recorded.

- Oral health: gums, teeth, dentures if relevant:
  - Not recorded.

- Ear exam including otoscopy:
  - Not recorded.

- Eye exam: visual acuity, pupil response, fundus if indicated:
  - Not recorded.

- Urinalysis: dipstick for protein, glucose, ketones, blood:
  - Not recorded.

Investigations (as indicated)

- Per transcript, no investigations were performed in the consult.
- Clinician recommended urgent hospital assessment to evaluate for venous thromboembolism (possible pulmonary embolism) given recent C‑section, acute shortness of breath, and tachycardia.
- Specific investigations (e.g., blood tests, imaging, ECG, D‑dimer) were not documented in the transcript.

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:
  - Patient advised to go promptly to hospital for assessment of possible clot.
  - Advised not to take codeine prior to presentation to hospital.
  - Advised to take necessary items for baby when going to hospital.

- Discuss patient health goals and priorities:
  - Not recorded.

- Schedule follow-up and recall appointments as needed:
  - Not recorded.

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (BP, respiratory rate, pulse rate with time interval, SpO2, temperature).
  - Anthropometric data (height, weight, BMI).
  - Immunisation review.
  - Detailed medication dosing/route/frequency (codeine dose not provided).
  - Smoking, alcohol, and substance use history.
  - Specific investigations/tests ordered or performed (bloods, imaging, ECG).
  - Postpartum/breastfeeding details and contraception discussion.

- Internal conflicts or contradictions from the transcript:
  - Pulse count: patient reported “30” but timing/duration of the count was not documented; clinician interpreted as “slightly fast” — ambiguity in numeric heart rate.
  - Medication use: patient states she has been taking codeine “fairly, fairly regularly” but also states “probably haven't taken it for a week” — minor conflict noted.

- Transcript quality notes:
  - Dialogue generally clear.
  - Several clinically relevant details not elicited or not recorded (e.g., exact pulse measurement interval, codeine dose, nature of ibuprofen allergy, objective vital signs, smoking/alcohol history, immunizations).
